lines.text: David blesses the LORD, his Rock, who trains his hands for war and is his shield and refuge.
David asks why the LORD thinks of man, who is like a breath with days like a passing shadow.
David asks the LORD to come down, flash His lightning, and rescue him from the deep waters and the grasp of foreigners.
David promises to sing a new song on a harp of ten strings to the One who gives victory to priests.
David pictures sons like plants and daughters like pillars adorning a temple, with walls unbroken and no captivity.
